config.title: Attribute selectors

intro.title: Attribute selectors
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple webpage that styles different types of input fields based on their HTML attributes. You will learn how to use CSS attribute selectors to target elements by their attributes, such as type, placeholder, or required status. The main technology involved is CSS, specifically using selectors like [type="text"] and [required] to apply specific styles. By the end, you'll understand how to precisely style elements without adding extra classes, making your CSS more efficient and maintainable.
intro.usecase: Attribute selectors are essential for styling dynamic web interfaces where elements share data attributes but need distinct visual treatments. In e-commerce filters, they target checkboxes with specific data-filter attributes to highlight active selections. Dashboard developers use them to style status indicators based on data-status attributes like 'pending' or 'approved'. They also simplify form validation by styling inputs with aria-invalid attributes, and help theme systems apply styles to elements with data-theme attributes.

objectives: Apply attribute selectors to style HTML elements based on their attributes
Construct CSS rules using exact attribute value matching
Configure partial attribute value matching with substring selectors
Implement attribute presence selectors to style elements with specific attributes
Manipulate styling based on attribute values that begin or end with specific strings
Integrate attribute selectors with other CSS selectors to create compound rules
Update existing CSS files to incorporate attribute-based styling techniques

steps.title: Create a basic HTML structure to style
steps.instruction: Create a simple HTML structure with various elements containing different attributes that we'll style in later steps. Add a <div> with class 'container' containing: a heading, a paragraph with a 'data-info' attribute, a link with a 'target' attribute, and an image with an 'alt' attribute.
steps.hint: You'll be writing HTML inside a CSS file - this is just for demonstration purposes. Use standard HTML tags with appropriate attributes.

steps.title: Style elements with a specific attribute
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that styles all elements with the 'data-highlight' attribute by giving them a yellow background color.
steps.hint: Use the attribute selector [data-highlight] followed by curly braces, then add a background-color property.
steps.expectedOutcome: Elements with the data-highlight attribute will have a yellow background when the CSS rule is applied.
successCriteria: A CSS rule using [data-highlight] selector exists and sets background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the exact attribute name 'data-highlight' and setting background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule doesn't match the expected structure. Review how attribute selectors work.

steps.title: Introduce attribute value selectors
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule that selects elements with a `data-highlight` attribute that has the exact value 'important' and sets their background color to yellow.
steps.hint: Use the attribute selector syntax [attribute="value"]. For example, [data-highlight="important"] will target elements where the data-highlight attribute equals 'important'.
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have a CSS rule that styles elements with data-highlight="important" with a yellow background.
successCriteria: A CSS rule exists that uses [data-highlight="important"] selector and sets background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using the exact syntax [data-highlight="important"] and setting background-color to yellow.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rule doesn't match the expected syntax. Review how attribute value selectors work: [attribute="value"].

steps.title: Style elements with exact attribute values
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style elements with the exact attribute value `data-type="warning"` by giving them a yellow background and bold text.
steps.hint: Use the attribute selector syntax [attribute="value"] to target elements with a specific attribute value. Inside the rule, set background-color to yellow and font-weight to bold.
steps.expectedOutcome: Elements with `data-type="warning"` will have a yellow background and bold text.
successCriteria: A CSS rule using [data-type="warning"] selector is added with background-color: yellow and font-weight: bold properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the selector, but make sure to include both background-color: yellow and font-weight: bold properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The rule is missing or incorrect. Use [data-type="warning"] selector with background-color: yellow and font-weight: bold.

steps.title: Introduce substring matching attribute selectors
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule using the substring matching attribute selector [data-type*="war"] to select elements whose data-type attribute contains the substring 'war'.
steps.hint: Use the syntax [attribute*="substring"] where * means 'contains'. This will match any element where the attribute value includes the specified substring.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule is added that uses [data-type*="war"] to select elements with data-type containing 'war'.
successCriteria: The CSS contains a rule with selector [data-type*="war"].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct selector syntax: [data-type*="war"]. The * operator matches any element where the attribute value contains the specified substring.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to add a CSS rule with the selector [data-type*="war"] to match elements whose data-type attribute contains the substring 'war'.

steps.title: Style elements with substring attribute values
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule using the substring matching attribute selector [data-type*="war"] to style elements whose data-type attribute contains 'war'.
steps.hint: Use the syntax [attribute*="value"] to select elements where the attribute value contains the specified substring anywhere within it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The CSS rule [data-type*="war"] should be added with style declarations inside.
successCriteria: A CSS rule with selector [data-type*="war"] exists and contains style properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using the correct selector syntax [data-type*="war"] and have added style properties inside the rule.
steps.feedbackWrong: The substring matching attribute selector rule is missing or incorrect. Remember to use [data-type*="war"] as the selector.

steps.title: Introduce prefix and suffix attribute selectors
steps.instruction: Add a new CSS rule that uses the prefix attribute selector [data-type^="war"] to style elements whose data-type attribute value starts with 'war'.
steps.hint: The prefix selector uses the ^= operator. Write a rule like [data-type^="war"] { /* styles */ }.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new CSS rule with the prefix selector [data-type^="war"] is added to the stylesheet.
successCriteria: The prefix selector [data-type^="war"] is correctly written and added as a new rule.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check the syntax. The prefix selector uses ^= and should target [data-type^="war"].
steps.feedbackWrong: The prefix selector wasn't added correctly. Remember to use [data-type^="war"] with the ^= operator.

steps.title: Style elements with prefix and suffix attribute values
steps.instruction: Add a CSS rule to style elements whose data-type attribute starts with 'war' using the prefix selector [data-type^="war"].
steps.hint: Use the attribute selector syntax [attribute^="value"] to target elements where the attribute value begins with the specified string.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule that styles elements with data-type values starting with 'war' (like 'warning' or 'warranty') will be created.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a valid [data-type^="war"] selector with at least one style property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your selector uses the correct prefix syntax [attribute^="value"] and includes at least one style property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The prefix selector wasn't implemented correctly. Review the syntax for targeting attribute values that start with a specific string.

steps.title: Combine attribute selectors for specific targeting
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS rule that combines two attribute selectors to target elements with both a 'data-type' attribute starting with 'war' and a 'data-highlight' attribute.
steps.hint: You can chain attribute selectors together without spaces between them to target elements that match all conditions.
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS rule that uses [data-type^="war"][data-highlight] to target elements matching both conditions.
successCriteria: A CSS rule is created with the selector [data-type^="war"][data-highlight].
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using both [data-type^="war"] and [data-highlight] selectors without spaces between them.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match the requirement. You need to create a selector that targets elements with both attributes.
